sourcedFrom: FIREARMS OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — DD4™ / DDM4® / DD5® — REV 1.4 (not printed as a year; the rights line reads "REV 1.4 Daniel Defense, LLC. All rights reserved.")
cleanIntro: Daniel Defense covers the DD5 in one book alongside its other rifles, and the strip below is the one that book publishes. ⚠ READ THE BRANCH: this manual prints TWO model-specific differences inside the strip itself, and they point in opposite directions. Your rifle is a DD5, so at step 8 the firing pin comes out WITH a firing pin return spring — account for it, because firing a DD5 with the pin installed and the spring left out is a hazard the manual calls out by name — and at step 9 the 90° cam-pin turn is explicitly NOT necessary on your rifle. Everything else is standard AR discipline done to Daniel Defense's own specification — a chamber brush worked five plunges and three full clockwise rotations, patches taken off at the muzzle rather than dragged back, no wire brush anywhere near the aluminium, and ammonia-based solutions removed or neutralised because they will permanently damage the rifle. The handguard stays on: Daniel Defense sends handguard removal to a gunsmith with factory torque figures.

steps.title: Selector to SAFE — and the hammer must be cocked first
steps.action: Point the rifle in a safe direction, finger off the trigger, hands away from the ejection port. Move the safety selector lever to SAFE. If it will not rotate, the hammer is down: cycle the charging handle once to cock it and the selector will then go to SAFE. On an AR the selector physically blocks the trigger only when there is a cocked hammer behind it.
steps.quote:
1. Set the safety selector lever to “SAFE.”
NOTE: The hammer must be cocked to place this firearm on “SAFE.”
steps.cite: FIREARMS OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — DD4™ / DDM4® / DD5® — REV 1.4 — Unloading — p.28

steps.title: Magazine out before the bolt moves
steps.action: Press the magazine catch and pull the magazine out of the well. Magazine first, chamber second — a round left in the chamber will fire whether or not the magazine is in the rifle, and stripping a magazine's worth of rounds out through the action is how people put a live round back into the chamber they just cleared.
steps.quote: 2. Press the magazine catch and remove the magazine.
steps.cite: FIREARMS OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — DD4™ / DDM4® / DD5® — REV 1.4 — Unloading — p.28

steps.title: Charging handle back, bolt catch in, and LOOK
steps.action: Draw the charging handle fully rearward and push in the lower portion of the bolt catch so the carrier locks back. Any chambered round is ejected as the bolt travels. Now look into the chamber through the ejection port and confirm with your eyes that it is empty — do not infer it from the fact that something flew out.
steps.quote:
3. Pull the charging handle to the rear and push in lower portion of bolt catch.
If a round was in the chamber, it should have been ejected. If the last round was fired, the bolt carrier group should already be locked to the rear provided a magazine was in place. 4. Look into the chamber through the ejection port to make sure the chamber is empty.
steps.cite: FIREARMS OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — DD4™ / DDM4® / DD5® — REV 1.4 — Unloading — p.28

steps.title: Release the bolt, and clear the magazine separately
steps.action: With the magazine out and the chamber confirmed empty, press the top of the bolt catch and let the carrier run forward. Then deal with the magazine away from the rifle: slide the remaining live rounds FORWARD out of it rather than levering them up over the feed lips, and put the ammunition somewhere else entirely before any tools come out.
steps.quote:
5. When the magazine is removed and the chamber is empty, push the top portion of the bolt catch to allow the bolt carrier group to return forward.
6. Remove remaining live rounds by sliding them forward out of the magazine. 7. Collect live ammunition for safe storage and spent cartridge cases for disposal.
steps.cite: FIREARMS OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — DD4™ / DDM4® / DD5® — REV 1.4 — Unloading — p.28

steps.title: Rear takedown pin out to its positive stop
steps.action: Lay the small parts out in order as they come off — Daniel Defense asks for that specifically, because an AR strip produces pins that roll. Press the rear takedown pin in from the LEFT side of the lower receiver and pull it out on the RIGHT until it reaches a positive stop. It is captive: it stops, it does not come out, and pulling harder only bends the detent.
steps.prose: To prevent loss of small components during stripping and cleaning, lay them out in an orderly fashion.
steps.quote:
2.	Press in the rear takedown pin from the left-hand side of lower receiver and 
pull the pin out on the right-hand side of the receiver until it comes to a  
positive stop.
steps.cite: FIREARMS OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — DD4™ / DDM4® / DD5® — REV 1.4 — Stripping for Cleaning — p.33

steps.title: Hinge the lower open, then pull the front pin if you want them apart
steps.action: Pivot the lower receiver down and away from the upper on the front pivot pin. That alone opens the rifle enough to get the bolt carrier out. If you would rather have two separate halves on the bench, press the FRONT takedown pin in from the left and pull it out on the right to its positive stop as well.
steps.quote:
3.	Pivot the lower receiver down and away from the upper receiver.
4.	If required for more convenience, completely separate the upper receiver from 
the lower receiver by pressing the front takedown pin from the left-hand side of 
the lower receiver and pulling out the pin on the right-hand side of the receiver 
until it comes to a positive stop.
steps.cite: FIREARMS OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — DD4™ / DDM4® / DD5® — REV 1.4 — Stripping for Cleaning — p.33

steps.title: Bolt carrier group out, then the charging handle down through the keyway
steps.action: Pull the charging handle rearward and draw the bolt carrier group straight out of the upper. Then take the charging handle itself back to the KEYWAY — the widened cut in its track — and drop it down and out. Order matters: the carrier holds the handle in its track, so the handle cannot come out first.
steps.quote:
5.	Pull charging handle to the rear and remove the bolt carrier group.
6.	Remove the charging handle by pulling it backward to the keyway and then 
down and out of the upper receiver.
steps.cite: FIREARMS OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — DD4™ / DDM4® / DD5® — REV 1.4 — Stripping for Cleaning — p.33

steps.title: Firing pin retaining pin out — RIGHT to LEFT
steps.action: Push the firing pin retaining pin in from the RIGHT side of the carrier and pull it out on the LEFT. It is a small cotter-style pin and it is the only thing holding the firing pin in. Drive it the wrong way and you will deform it against the carrier's counterbore.
steps.quote:
7.	Push in the firing pin retaining pin from right to left of the bolt carrier group and 
remove the pin by pulling it out to the left.
steps.cite: FIREARMS OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — DD4™ / DDM4® / DD5® — REV 1.4 — Stripping for Cleaning — p.33

steps.title: Bolt face UP, firing pin AND its return spring out — DD5 only
steps.action: Tilt the bolt face upward so the firing pin cannot slide out under gravity, then draw the firing pin out of the rear of the carrier — and with it the FIRING PIN RETURN SPRING, which is fitted to the DD5 and not to Daniel Defense's smaller-frame rifles. Account for that spring now. Reassembling a DD5 with the firing pin in and the return spring left on the bench is a named hazard in this manual.
steps.prose: The return spring is the single most consequential DD5-versus-DDM4 difference in this strip, and it is easy to lose because it comes away with the pin rather than staying in the carrier.
steps.quote:
8.	Tilt the bolt face up and remove the firing pin (and firing pin return spring—for 
DD5 only).
steps.cite: FIREARMS OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — DD4™ / DDM4® / DD5® — REV 1.4 — Stripping for Cleaning — p.33
steps.warn:
IF YOU INSTALL THE FIRING PIN WITHOUT THE FIRING PIN RETURN 
SPRING AND LATER ATTEMPT TO FIRE THE FIREARM, DAMAGE TO THE FIREARM 
OR INJURY MAY RESULT (DD5 ONLY).

steps.title: Cam pin straight out — no 90° turn on a DD5
steps.action: Lift the cam pin up and out of the bolt and carrier. On the DD5 you do NOT turn it through 90° first: the manual says the rotation step is not necessary on this rifle, and the DD5's bolt geometry lets the pin come straight out. If it resists, push the bolt in toward the carrier to unload it rather than twisting.
steps.aside:
9.	Push the bolt in toward the carrier until bolt rotates and comes to a stop, then 
turn the bolt cam pin through 90° (not necessary on DD5).
steps.quote: 10.	Remove the cam pin by lifting it out and away from the bolt and bolt carrier.
steps.cite: FIREARMS OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — DD4™ / DDM4® / DD5® — REV 1.4 — Stripping for Cleaning — p.33

steps.title: Bolt forward out of the carrier — field strip complete
steps.action: Pull the bolt forward out of the front of the carrier. The DD5 is now in its published parts: upper, lower, charging handle, carrier, bolt, cam pin, firing pin and its return spring and the firing pin retaining pin. Daniel Defense's instruction is explicit — do not strip the firearm further than this; anything more goes to Servicing and Repairing. In particular the handguard stays on: if it genuinely has to come off, that is a gunsmith job with torque specifications from the factory.
steps.quote: 11.	 Pull the bolt forward and remove it from the bolt carrier.
steps.cite: FIREARMS OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — DD4™ / DDM4® / DD5® — REV 1.4 — Stripping for Cleaning — p.33
steps.warn:
Do not strip your firearm further than previously described. If additional 
maintenance is required, see "Servicing and Repairing" later in this instruction manual.

steps.title: Cold rifle, gloves, goggles, mask, ventilation
steps.action: Let the rifle cool to room temperature before any solvent touches it — a hot barrel flashes solvent off and bakes residue in. Wear chemical-resistant gloves, eye protection and a mask, and work with real ventilation. Daniel Defense also warns that ammonia-based solutions must be removed or neutralised afterwards or they will permanently damage the rifle.
steps.quote: Be sure to remove or neutralize any ammonia-based cleaning solutions from the firearm as they can cause permanent damage.
steps.cite: FIREARMS OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — DD4™ / DDM4® / DD5® — REV 1.4 — How to Clean — p.35
steps.warn:
ALLOW FIREARM TO COOL TO ROOM TEMPERATURE BEFORE 
ATTEMPTING CLEANING/MAINTENANCE.

steps.title: Patches from the CHAMBER end, off at the muzzle, never back through
steps.action: Put a cotton flannel patch on the rod, start it at the chamber and push it out of the muzzle — then take the dirty patch OFF at the muzzle rather than dragging it back through. Fresh patch each pass until the last one comes out clean. Keep the rod off the muzzle crown as you work; wear there costs accuracy permanently and cannot be undone.
steps.caution:
NOTE: Avoid contact between the cleaning rod and the muzzle as resultant wear  
will greatly reduce accuracy.
steps.quote:
2.	Attach a cotton flannel patch to end of the cleaning rod, insert it in the 
chamber and pass the rod and patch down through the barrel and out the 
muzzle. Remove used patches at muzzle to avoid pulling it back through the 
bore. Repeat, changing patches with each pass through the barrel, until the 
last patch comes out clean.
steps.cite: FIREARMS OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — DD4™ / DDM4® / DD5® — REV 1.4 — How to Clean — p.36

steps.title: Bore brush only if the barrel is still dirty — and never reverse it inside
steps.action: Inspect the barrel. If it is clean, skip straight to wiping down and oiling. If it is not, put a nylon bore brush on the rod, dip it in solution and scrub — passing the brush ALL THE WAY THROUGH before you reverse direction. Changing direction with the brush still in the bore is how a brush gets stuck, and getting one out damages the barrel.
steps.quote:
4.	Attach nylon wire-bristle bore-cleaning brush to cleaning rod and dip brush in 
firearm-cleaning solution. Thoroughly scrub out barrel, passing the brush all 
the way through before reversing the movement. If you try to change direction 
with the brush in barrel, the brush can get stuck and cause damage to barrel.
steps.cite: FIREARMS OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — DD4™ / DDM4® / DD5® — REV 1.4 — How to Clean — p.36

steps.title: Chamber brush: five plunges, three full clockwise rotations
steps.action: Fit the larger chamber brush, dip it in solution and clean the chamber to a specification rather than by feel — a minimum of five plunge strokes and three full 360-degree clockwise rotational strokes. The locking-lug recesses in an AR chamber are where carbon builds into a hard ring, and rotation is the only motion that reaches them.
steps.quote:
5.	Attach the larger chamber-cleaning brush to the cleaning rod, dip the brush in 
bore-cleaning solution, and clean the chamber. Use a minimum of five plunge 
strokes and three 360° clockwise rotational strokes.
steps.cite: FIREARMS OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — DD4™ / DDM4® / DD5® — REV 1.4 — How to Clean — p.37

steps.title: The carbon list: gas tube area, lugs, rings, cam pin, extractor lip, inside the carrier
steps.action: With an all-purpose nylon brush and solution, clean the carbon and powder residue from a specific list of places: around the gas tube in the upper receiver, the bolt locking lugs, the bolt rings, the firing pin, the bolt cam pin, the LIP of the extractor and the inside of the bolt carrier. That extractor lip is the one people skip, and a carboned extractor lip is the classic cause of a failure to extract.
steps.quote:
7.	Use an all-purpose nylon cleaning brush and firearm-cleaning solution to clean 
all carbon and powder residue from around the gas tube in the upper receiver, 
bolt locking lugs, bolt rings, firing pin, bolt cam pin, lip of the extractor, and 
inside the bolt carrier group.
steps.cite: FIREARMS OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — DD4™ / DDM4® / DD5® — REV 1.4 — How to Clean — p.37
steps.warn:
Do not use a wire brush on aluminum surfaces such as the upper and lower 
receivers and the handguards.

steps.title: Wipe dry, INSPECT, then oil the bore according to what happens next
steps.action: Wipe every component clean and dry and actually inspect it for wear, corrosion and mechanical damage — this is the moment the rifle tells you something is wrong, and anything found must be fixed before it is fired again. Then a lightly oiled flannel patch once through the barrel. If the rifle is going into storage, leave that film; if it is going back to use, run a dry patch through the barrel and chamber and take as much of it out as you can.
steps.aside:
8.	Wipe all components clean and dry and inspect them for excessive wear, 
corrosion or mechanical damage. If any of these conditions are discovered, have 
them corrected before firing again.
steps.quote:
9.	Lightly dampen a flannel patch with gun oil and pass it once through the 
barrel, leaving a thin film of oil on the inside surface. Leave this film of oil on 
the surface if firearm is to be stored. If it is not being stored, or if it is being 
removed from storage for use, pass the dry patch through the barrel and 
chamber to remove as much oil as possible.
steps.cite: FIREARMS OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — DD4™ / DDM4® / DD5® — REV 1.4 — How to Clean — p.37

steps.title: Check for stray bristles, lubricate the named points, remove fingerprints
steps.action: Before anything goes back together, check that no flannel threads or brush bristles have lodged anywhere in the rifle — a bristle in the gas tube or under the extractor causes a stoppage that looks like a broken part. Then lubricate the points Daniel Defense lists, and finally take the solution, oil and FINGERPRINTS off the outside; finger moisture left on steel starts corrosion on its own.
steps.quote:
10.	Check that flannel or brush bristles have not become lodged in any part of 
firearm, then lightly lubricate (See Section 5.4).
11.	 Remove any gun-cleaning solution, oil, and fingerprints from the outside 
surfaces of the firearm. (Finger moisture, if left, could start a corrosion process.)
steps.cite: FIREARMS OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — DD4™ / DDM4® / DD5® — REV 1.4 — How to Clean — p.37

steps.title: Cleaning interval, and the loaded-carry rule
steps.action: Before firing, the barrel and chamber must be clean and DRY. After firing, clean as soon as you can. Unfired, once or twice a year in a temperate climate and as often as weekly in a tropical one. And if the rifle is carried loaded, Daniel Defense wants it unloaded and cleaned at least once a month regardless of round count.
steps.aside: IF YOU CARRY A LOADED FIREARM, UNLOAD it and clean when necessary and at least once a month. If you get your firearm wet, clean it as soon as possible.
steps.quote: BEFORE FIRING, make sure that the barrel and the chamber are clean and dry. After firing, clean your firearm as soon as possible so that the job will be easier and there will be less opportunity for corrosion to start.
steps.cite: FIREARMS OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — DD4™ / DDM4® / DD5® — REV 1.4 — When to Clean — p.35

deepSteps.title: Handguard: air and lubricant only — removal is a gunsmith job
deepSteps.action: The DD5's handguard is not a user-serviceable item. If dirt or debris has collected in or around it, blow it out with compressed air and lubricate as needed, and stop there. Daniel Defense states that if removal is genuinely necessary the rifle goes to a qualified and competent gunsmith, and that the removal, installation and TORQUE specifications are available from the factory — which is the tell that the barrel-nut interface is a controlled joint, not a hand-fit one.
deepSteps.aside:
NOTE: Removal is not necessary unless dirt has accumulated in or around  
the handguard.
deepSteps.quote:
c.	If removal of handguard is deemed necessary, please take firearm to a 
qualified and competent gunsmith.
deepSteps.cite: FIREARMS OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — DD4™ / DDM4® / DD5® — REV 1.4 — Stripping for Cleaning — p.33

deepSteps.title: Buttstock off the receiver extension
deepSteps.action: Push the buttstock's release lever up and run the stock fully to its longest position, then pull the tabs of the buttstock latch, compressing the latch spring completely, and slide the stock off the rear of the receiver extension. Compressing the latch fully is what clears the detent from the tube's position slots; half-compressed, the stock drags and people force it.
deepSteps.quote:
13.	Remove the buttstock from lower receiver (if equipped):
a.	Push the release lever up and extend the buttstock fully.
b.	Pull tabs of buttstock latch, compressing spring completely, and slide 
buttstock off the receiver extension.
deepSteps.cite: FIREARMS OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — DD4™ / DDM4® / DD5® — REV 1.4 — Stripping for Cleaning — p.34

deepSteps.title: Buffer and action spring — thumb on the buffer BEFORE the retainer pin
deepSteps.action: This is the step that catches people. Depress the buffer and KEEP the pressure on it, because it is under action-spring tension and will launch across the room the instant the buffer retainer pin drops. With the buffer held, depress the buffer retainer pin so the buffer and action spring can move forward, then depress the hammer so they can continue forward and come completely out of the receiver extension.
deepSteps.prose: The hammer is what blocks the last part of the travel, which is why depressing it is a separate instruction rather than an afterthought.
deepSteps.quote:
14.	Depress the buffer, maintaining pressure as the buffer is under spring tension, 
to prevent it from being ejected when the buffer retainer pin is depressed. 
Depress the buffer retainer pin to permit the buffer and the action spring to 
move forward. Depress the hammer to allow the action spring and the buffer 
assembly to continue moving forward and be completely removed from the 
receiver extension.
deepSteps.cite: FIREARMS OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — DD4™ / DDM4® / DD5® — REV 1.4 — Stripping for Cleaning — p.34
deepSteps.warn:
Do not strip your firearm further than previously described. If additional 
maintenance is required, see "Servicing and Repairing" later in this instruction manual.

deepSteps.title: Clean the buffer, spring and tube; no wire brushes on aluminium
deepSteps.action: Wipe the buffer body, the action spring and the inside of the receiver extension clean with solution and a nylon brush, then dry them. The receiver extension is aluminium — use a small nylon brush or a flannel patch on it and never a wire brush, which scratches the bore the buffer has to run in and makes the rifle noisier and rougher, not cleaner.
deepSteps.quote:
Do not use a wire brush on aluminum surfaces such as the upper and lower 
receivers and the handguards. If cleaning is necessary, avoid scratches and wear by using a 
small nylon brush or flannel patch.
deepSteps.cite: FIREARMS OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — DD4™ / DDM4® / DD5® — REV 1.4 — How to Clean — p.37

deepSteps.title: Buffer and spring back in first, then the stock
deepSteps.action: Reassembly of this branch goes in its own order and Daniel Defense prints it: the buffer and action spring go into the receiver extension FIRST, and the buffer retaining pin must then be preventing any forward movement of them. Only after that does the buttstock go back on — pull the release lever down and push the stock forward onto the receiver extension.
deepSteps.quote:
a.	 Insert the buffer/action spring and buffer into the receiver extension/ 
buffer tube on the rear of the lower receiver. The buffer retaining pin 
should prevent any forward movement of the buffer/action spring.
b.	 Install the buttstock onto the lower receiver. Pull the release lever down 
and push the buttstock forward on the receiver extension/buffer tube.
deepSteps.cite: FIREARMS OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — DD4™ / DDM4® / DD5® — REV 1.4 — How to Clean, Reassemble the firearm — p.37

deepSteps.title: Preservation for the environment the rifle actually lives in
deepSteps.action: Finish the deep clean by protecting the steel: barrel, gas block, muzzle device, pins, forward assist and ejection port cover. Coastal salt air, high humidity and dust all demand more aggressive preservation than a dry climate does, and a preservative works by putting a barrier between the steel and the contaminants rather than by cleaning anything.
deepSteps.quote: Areas with excessive humidity, salt (coastal areas), dust, etc., will require more aggressive preservation efforts.
deepSteps.cite: FIREARMS OPERATION & SAFETY MANUAL — DD4™ / DDM4® / DD5® — REV 1.4 — Lubricating/Preservation — p.38

cleaning.name: Barrel and chamber
tasks: Rifle cooled to room temperature first.
Cotton flannel patches from the CHAMBER end, removed at the muzzle, fresh patch each pass until clean.
Nylon bore brush only if the barrel is still dirty — all the way through before reversing.
Chamber brush: minimum five plunge strokes and three 360° clockwise rotational strokes.
Keep the cleaning rod off the muzzle crown.
Bore clean and DRY before firing.

cleaning.name: Bolt carrier group
tasks: Carbon and powder residue off the bolt locking lugs, the bolt rings and the firing pin.
Bolt cam pin and the LIP of the extractor — the extractor lip is the commonly skipped one.
Inside of the bolt carrier itself.
Around the gas tube where it enters the upper receiver.
Wipe dry and inspect for wear, corrosion or damage before anything is oiled.

cleaning.name: Receivers and handguard
tasks: NO wire brush on aluminium — small nylon brush or flannel patch only.
Compressed air through the handguard if dirt has accumulated; do not remove it.
Check no flannel threads or brush bristles are lodged anywhere before reassembly.

cleaning.name: Lubrication points
tasks: Bolt carrier group: carrier rails, cam pin, bolt lugs, extractor and extractor pin, gas rings, firing pin, retaining pin, ejector.
Fire control group: hammer, trigger, pins, disconnector, selector.
Magazine catch, bolt catch, bolt release, ejection port cover, forward assist.
Takedown pin, pivot pin, buffer retaining pin, buffer spring, buttstock latch, charging handle.
Sight aperture pivot point, sight adjustment wheel, front sight detent.
High-quality gun oil only; check with the maker that it suits the application.

cleaning.name: Preservation and exterior
tasks: Remove all cleaning solution, oil and FINGERPRINTS from outside surfaces.
Neutralise or remove any ammonia-based solution — it causes permanent damage.
Protect the steel: barrel, gas block, muzzle device, pins, forward assist, ejection port cover.
Humid, coastal or dusty environments need more aggressive preservation.
Magazine care: refer to the magazine manufacturer, not to this book.

reassembly: Buffer and action spring into the receiver extension; the buffer retaining pin must prevent forward movement of them.
Buttstock onto the lower: release lever down, stock pushed forward onto the receiver extension.
Bolt into the bolt carrier with the CHAMFERED edge of the bolt body — where the cam pin sits — facing DOWNWARD; the cam pin enters from the opposite side of the chamfer.
Cross-check: the extractor should be oriented to the RIGHT side of the bolt carrier.
Cam pin into the bolt and bolt carrier.
DD5: the cam pin does NOT need the 90° rotation the smaller-frame rifles require.
Firing pin AND the firing pin return spring back in — the return spring is fitted to the DD5 and leaving it out is a named hazard.
Firing pin retaining pin back through the carrier.
Charging handle into its track through the keyway, then the bolt carrier group in behind it.
Upper closed onto the lower; front pivot pin then rear takedown pin pushed home.
Confirm the cam pin is properly installed before the rifle is closed up — the manual makes this a named check.
fncheck: With the rifle proven empty, magazine out and muzzle in a safe direction: cycle the charging handle several times and confirm the carrier runs fully forward and locks. Confirm the bolt catch holds the carrier back and releases cleanly. Cock the hammer, set the selector to SAFE and confirm the trigger will not release it; move to SEMI and confirm it does. Check both takedown pins are fully home. Verify the cam pin is installed — the manual warns that firing without it damages the rifle — and that the firing pin return spring is fitted, which is a DD5-specific check. Last, confirm the bore and chamber are clean, dry and free of patches or bristles before loading.
